identity.name: Ilorin Emirate
alt_names: Ilorin Emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate

land.text: Ilorin and the north of Oyo, where the Kakanfo Afonja rebelled with Shehu Alimi

predecessors.note: Ilorin page: 'when the local Kakanfo (field marshal) named Afonja rebelled, supported by the Fulani Shehu Alimi'; the Ilorin Emirate page: 'In approximately 1810, Shehu Alimi and Afonja form alliance to repel the punitive forces of Oyo'.

land.text: Ilorin, 'occupied by the Royal Niger Company in 1897'

successors.note: 'its lands were incorporated into the British Northern Nigeria Protectorate in 1900' (Ilorin page); the emirate continued under its emirs (Sulaymanu dan Aliyu 1896 - 14 January 1914).

capitals.name: Ilorin
capitals.note: The gazetteer's Ilorin point; the Ilorin Emirate page gives coordinates but no capital.

correction.text: Ilorin and the north of Oyo; Ilorin's jihad 'toward the sea' was 'stopped at Oshogbo in 1840 by the army of Ibadan'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Neither page gives the emirate's boundaries ('Any description of the emirate's boundaries or total territory' is not given; the 765 km2 on the Ilorin page is the modern metropolis); a 60 km circle round Ilorin (the Oyo dossier's choice for its 1817 loss) stands for it. The reach to Oshogbo is not drawn.

region.text: Ilorin and the north of Oyo

ledger.note: 1817: Afonja rebels at Ilorin with Shehu Alimi. 'when the local Kakanfo (field marshal) named Afonja rebelled, supported by the Fulani Shehu Alimi' (the section gloss gives 1817; the Ilorin Emirate page has the alliance 'In approximately 1810').

region.text: the Ilorin emirate under the Sokoto Caliphate

ledger.note: 1823: Abd al-Salam 'pledged allegiance to the Sokoto Caliphate in 1823' (Ilorin page); 'Ilorin became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate under the authority of Gwandu' (Emirate page, undated; the sokoto-caliphate dossier records a 1824 gain). Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added so that the emirate's place in the caliphate is drawn.

1838: Ibadan defeats Ilorin. 'Ilorin's southward expansion effectively ended in 1838 when Ibadan, an Oyo successor state decisively defeated Ilorin'; the Ilorin page has Abd al-Salam's jihad 'stopped at Oshogbo in 1840 by the army of Ibadan'.
1840: Ilorin's southward jihad ends at Oshogbo. 'led the jihad toward the sea but was ultimately stopped at Oshogbo in 1840 by the army of Ibadan.'

region.text: the Ilorin emirate under the Sokoto Caliphate

ledger.note: 1897: the tie to Sokoto ends when Ilorin 'was occupied by the Royal Niger Company in 1897' (Ilorin page). Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the close of the 1823 vassal_start.
1897: the Royal Niger Company occupies Ilorin. The city 'was occupied by the Royal Niger Company in 1897' (no month on the page).
1897: Ilorin ceases to be an independent emirate; its lands were 'incorporated into the British Northern Nigeria Protectorate in 1900'.

wars.name: Ilorin-Ibadan wars
wars.outcome: Ibadan stopped Ilorin's southward expansion: 'decisively defeated Ilorin' in 1838 (Emirate page), the jihad 'stopped at Oshogbo in 1840' (Ilorin page).
wars.note: The Battles of Ogbomosho (the 1830s) and Pamo are named without years.

wars.name: Royal Niger Company occupation of Ilorin
wars.outcome: The Royal Niger Company occupied Ilorin in 1897; the emirate was brought under the Northern Protectorate 'through diplomacy and applying minimal force' (Emirate page, undated).

sources.title: Ilorin Emirate
sources.note: Alliance of Alimi and Afonja about 1810; southward expansion ended by Ibadan in 1838; rulers table (Abdusalami 1824-1842, Sulaymanu 1896-14 January 1914); brought under the Northern Protectorate by minimal force; no founding date, capital or area.

sources.title: Ilorin
sources.note: Afonja's rebellion (1817 gloss), Abd al-Salam and Sokoto allegiance 1823, Oshogbo 1840, occupied by the Royal Niger Company 1897, Northern Nigeria Protectorate 1900.

notes: The Ilorin Emirate has no Cliopatria row (the Oyo dossier, af-04-a, uses ilorin-emirate as counterpart of its 1817 loss and its 1835 dissolve). Two pages opened. The year 1817 is the Ilorin page's gloss for Afonja's rebellion (the quoted sentence itself carries no year); the Emirate page says 'approximately 1810' for the alliance. Disagreements: 1838 (Emirate page) vs 1840 (Ilorin page) for the end of the southward expansion; Abdusalami from 1823 (Ilorin page, allegiance to Sokoto) vs 1824 (rulers table). The destruction of Oyo-Ile in 1835 is on the Oyo page (not opened here) and is not repeated. The emirate's status as an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate is undated on the Emirate page; the Sokoto dossier (af-03) should carry the vassal event. The Royal Niger Company dossier (this batch) carries the mirror gain.
